witness.edition: Edmundo Burke, Indagacion filosófica sobre el orígen de nuestras ideas acerca de lo sublime y lo bello, translated by Juan de la Dehesa Rubiano (Alcalá: Oficina de la Real Universidad, 1807), p. 1.
witness.licence: Public-domain historical translation; author and translator died more than 100 years ago, and this edition was published in 1807.
witness.attribution: Edmund Burke, translated into Spanish by Juan de la Dehesa Rubiano, Alcalá, 1807, p. 1.
witness.normalization: Preserve historical spelling, accents and punctuation as printed; normalize line-break hyphenation and whitespace.

usa.law: The named Spanish translation was published in 1807, before 1931; 17 USC 304. https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap3.html#304

eu.law: The author died in 1797 and the named translator in 1839, both more than 70 years ago; Directive 2006/116/EC article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2006/116/oj

russia.law: Both the author (d. 1797) and translator (d. 1839) died more than 70 years and the conservative wartime extension ago; Russian Civil Code article 1281. https://www.consultant.ru/document/cons_doc_LAW_64629/675b81f0bc9b8ecd68ea332ecfd9d1562541fb98/

Taste p79.text: Puede parecer á primera vista, que nos diferenciamos mucho unos de otros en nuestros raciocinios, y no menos en nuestros placeres; pero no obstante esta diferencia, que en mi concepto tiene mas de apariencia que de realidad, es probable que la regla de la razon y del gusto sea una misma en todas las criaturas humanas.

transcription.reason: The 1807 PDF is a photographed print without a usable text layer; the sentence was manually read from the source-bound printed page, preserving the historical accents and the semicolon after placeres.
transcription.original_text: Puede parecer á primera vista, que nos diferenciamos mucho unos de otros en nuestros raciocinios, y no menos en nuestros placeres; pero no obstante esta diferencia, que en mi concepto tiene mas de apariencia que de realidad, es probable que la regla de la razon y del gusto sea una misma en todas las criaturas humanas.

Taste p79.alignment: The printed Spanish introductory sentence corresponds to the English On Taste opening: apparent difference in reasoning and pleasure, qualified as more apparent than real, and the probable common standard of reason and taste.

I read the exact source-bound second page image and the original English printed page. The full sentence preserves apparent difference and the probable common standard. The Spanish punctuation is verified: á primera vista, mas and razon without accents, semicolon after placeres, and the final stop. The line breaks are normalized and the initial P is decorative, with no meaningful emphasis lost.
